issues.name: fix-recommend-workflow-empty-rationale-crash
issues.description: intent assess throws an uncaught ZodError (rationale array must have >=1 items) whenever recommendWorkflow() pushes to stages via the ARCHITECTURE_REQUIRED/DESIGN_REQUIRED/RESEARCH_REQUIRED/PLANNING_REQUIRED label branches without also pushing a rationale string - those four branches never populate rationale, only the CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED and readiness===ready branches do. Repro: an intent with unknowns:[] and objective set, readiness came back ready/confidence 100/blockers:[], but triage also included DEFERRED (see the sibling deferred-keyword issue) alongside ARCHITECTURE_REQUIRED/DESIGN_REQUIRED. Because DEFERRED skipped the ready branch and CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED was absent, stages ended up non-empty ([architecture, design]) with rationale=[] , failing workflowRecommendationSchema and exiting 1 instead of returning a result. Reported by Virdua project via Claude Code, confirmed against installed dist/cli.js source. Fix: attach a rationale string to every stage-pushing branch (research/architecture/design/planning), not just the three special-cased ones.

issues.name: fix-intent-triage-deferred-conflict-keyword-false-positives
issues.description: The deferred and conflict KEYWORDS regexes in src/intent/triage.ts are matched against searchableText()'s single space-joined blob of raw+objective+every array field, with no field or sentence boundary. deferred: /\b(later|defer|deferred|someday|backlog)\b/i fires on any use of the common word later even in legitimate future-scope language (e.g. a later, additive channel), incorrectly setting DEFERRED. conflict: /\b(always|never)\b.*\b(?:unless|except|but)\b/i uses unbounded .* so it matches across the entire remaining document after the first always/never, flagging CONFLICT_DETECTED on completely unrelated sentences dozens of words apart (e.g. never in one requirement, but in an unrelated assumption several sentences later). Reproduced live across 5 separate Virdua intent drafts (architecture, design, data, security, development-plan gates) - every single one of them tripped one or both regexes on ordinary, non-contradictory prose, forcing manual rewording each time to work around it. This is high-frequency, not an edge case. Fix: drop later from the deferred list (keep defer/deferred/someday/backlog, which are much more deliberate signals), and scope conflict to a single sentence or bounded word-window rather than the full joined blob.

issues.name: add-bootstrap-approve-verb-for-manifest-artifacts
issues.description: bootstrap gates and bootstrap status are a pure literal read of .autoforge/bootstrap/manifest.json's artifacts[].status field (BOOTSTRAP_GATES = [architecture, design, data, security], checking status === approved). Nothing else in the CLI ever writes approved into that file: bootstrap vision-approve only writes vision-approvals.json (not manifest.json); intent assess --persist writes to .autoforge/planning/; workflow start/advance writes to .autoforge/workflows/; design import/validate writes to the design store. None of them touch the manifest. We ran complete, genuine intent-assess + workflow-start/advance cycles (ending status: completed) for all four gated artifacts on the Virdua project, and bootstrap gates still reported everything pending throughout, because manifest.json literally never changes from bootstrap scaffold's initial all-planned output. We had to hand-edit manifest.json directly via a text editor to flip status to approved for each of the 6 artifacts we touched (architecture, design, data, security, development-plan, tasks) - fragile, unvalidated, and completely undiscoverable without reading dist/cli.js source. This makes the entire bootstrap-gates feature silently decorative once a project moves past bootstrap vision. Fix: add autoforge bootstrap approve <artifact-id> that validates the id, writes status: approved plus approvedAt into manifest.json, and optionally accepts --evidence <path> (a workflow run id or planning artifact path) to validate real backing work exists before approving.

issues.name: unify-intent-and-workflow-kind-vocabularies
issues.description: intent assess --kind uses readinessWorkKindSchema = enum([implementation, research, architecture, design, planning]), while workflow start <id> <kind> uses a completely different workflowKindSchema = enum([feature-development, bug-fix, research, design-create, design-critique, architecture-change, validation]). research is the only value shared between them. A user who just ran intent assess --kind architecture naturally tries workflow start my-run architecture next - it fails with a bare Usage: ... string, no indication of why or what the valid values are (the real value needed is architecture-change, an unrelated string). Every pairing (architecture<->architecture-change, design<->design-create/design-critique, planning<->nothing, implementation<->feature-development/bug-fix) requires the user to already know both schemas exist and differ. This is the second confirmed instance of the same enum-drift failure mode as the earlier agents-list-vs-contract-generate capability mismatch (fixed in 0.16.3) - worth a structural fix (single source-of-truth vocabulary module + a test asserting shared enums stay in sync or have an explicit mapping) rather than another one-off patch. Fix at minimum: on an invalid workflow <kind>, enumerate the actual valid values in the error message instead of the generic usage string.

issues.name: add-data-and-security-work-kinds-to-intent-and-workflow
issues.description: readinessWorkKindSchema (intent assess --kind) only has implementation/research/architecture/design/planning - no data or security value exists at all. workflowKindSchema (workflow start <kind>) has no data/security-flavored value either (closest available is architecture-change). But bootstrap's own manifest treats data and security as 2 of exactly 4 gated artifacts (BOOTSTRAP_GATES = [architecture, design, data, security]). There is no supported way to run a properly-labeled data or security intent assessment or workflow. We worked around this on the Virdua project by passing --kind architecture for both a data-schema/retention intent and an authn/authz intent - readiness scoring came back reasonable in both cases (ready, confidence 100), but the workKind field in every output is now misleadingly labeled architecture for what is actually data-modeling or security work, and the workaround will need to be repeated by every future user closing these same two gates. This is a genuine capability gap, not just cosmetic naming drift: 2 of bootstrap's 4 gated artifacts cannot be assessed through their own vocabulary. Fix: extend readinessWorkKindSchema and workflowKindSchema to include data and security as first-class work kinds, ideally as part of the broader shared-vocabulary fix (see the intent/workflow enum unification issue), so all 4 gated artifacts have a real, correctly-labeled path through intent assess -> workflow start/advance.

issues.name: surface-real-errors-instead-of-bare-catch-in-workflow-command
issues.description: runWorkflowCommand in src/commands/workflow.ts wraps its entire action dispatch (start/show/advance/handoff) in a bare catch {} that discards any thrown error - including a fully diagnosable ZodError like workflowKindSchema.parse(kind) rejecting an invalid enum value - and converts it into the same generic usage string used for genuine argument-count/shape mistakes. This directly worsened the intent-vs-workflow kind-mismatch issue: the real error (Invalid enum value. Expected feature-development|bug-fix|...|architecture-change, received architecture) was fully descriptive but got thrown away in favor of a bare Usage: ... line giving zero indication the problem was specifically an invalid <kind> value. The same bare-catch/swallowed-error shape was previously implicated in a contract generate claude/grok bug report (a real thrown compatibility error became a generic exit-code-2 usage error). We also observed a similar unhelpful bare exit code 2 from autoforge use with no arguments (Project: '<alias>' - just exit 2, no message). Fix: distinguish ZodError and other domain errors with a real .message from genuine usage/arg-shape mistakes, and print the real error to stderr - either always or behind --verbose/AUTOFORGE_DEBUG=1. Audit for the same bare catch {} pattern in other command files (e.g. the use command entrypoint), since it appears to be a repeated idiom, not isolated to workflow.ts.

issues.name: namespace-persisted-planning-artifacts-to-avoid-silent-overwrite
issues.description: intent assess --artifact <kind> --persist writes to a fixed path .autoforge/planning/<kind>.json, derived from the artifact kind alone - no run id, timestamp, or source-intent name in the path. Running --artifact technical-plan --persist a second time for unrelated work that also happens to produce a technical-plan-kind artifact silently overwrites the first file, with no warning, confirmation prompt, or diff. Reproduced 4 times in a row on the Virdua project: persisting a technical-plan artifact for the design, data, security, and development-plan bootstrap gates each clobbered the previous gate's technical-plan.json in place. We only recovered the earlier content because it had already been committed to git (git show HEAD~1:.autoforge/planning/technical-plan.json); a user who ran two passes before committing, or who doesn't use git at all, would lose the first artifact permanently and silently. This is a 100% reproduction rate across every applicable run this session, not an edge case. Fix: namespace persisted artifacts by more than kind alone - e.g. .autoforge/planning/<kind>/<source-fingerprint-or-intent-basename>.json - or at minimum refuse to overwrite an existing file without --force, and print a diff or confirmation when a write would clobber one. The sourceFingerprint value already computed and embedded in each artifact's JSON body is exactly what should be part of the persisted path.

issues.name: improve-generated-user-stories-artifact-quality
issues.description: The --artifact user-stories generator (intent assess, generatorVersion 0.8.0-planning.1) mechanically templates every requirement string verbatim into 'As a user, I want <requirement text, unedited> so the stated objective is achieved,' with no actor extraction, no rephrasing into real story shape, and no splitting of compound requirements. Output is syntactically a user story but not a useful one - e.g. 'As a user, I want sequence the authorization middleware and session/token handling immediately after the data model, since the matching engine and candidate UI both depend on having real auth boundaries to build against. so the stated objective is achieved.' reads as barely grammatical boilerplate wrapped around the original requirement rather than a real decomposed story. Observed generating user-stories for the Virdua development-plan gate. This is a quality/usefulness gap, not a crash - lower priority than the correctness issues, but worth fixing since --persist artifacts are meant to be immediately actionable starting points for implementation, and right now they require significant manual rewriting before they are.

issues.name: publish-introspectable-json-schemas-for-file-accepting-commands
issues.description: Every command that takes a <json-file> argument (bootstrap discover, intent assess, intent register, research register, workflow handoff, design import, etc.) has an input schema that must be reverse-engineered by grepping the minified dist/cli.js bundle for z.object({...}) definitions near known strings, since none of it is documented in the GitHub repo README or docs/AUTOFORGE_AGENT_SETUP_GUIDE.md. We had to do this from source for discoverySchema, triageIntentSchema, and workflowHandoffSchema across this engagement. For a CLI whose primary interaction model for non-trivial commands is hand it a JSON file, this is a real and recurring onboarding cost - every new agent/session doing this kind of work re-derives the same schemas from source. Fix: ship a schemas/ directory in the published package (JSON Schema or raw Zod shape exported at build time) covering every file-accepting command, or add a --schema introspection flag, e.g. autoforge intent assess --schema prints the exact expected input shape.

issues.name: document-bootstrap-to-intent-workflow-design-planning-relationship
issues.description: bootstrap's tracked artifact list (vision, problem, users, use-cases, user-stories, flows, research, architecture, design, data, security, development-plan, tasks, per bootstrap status) strongly implies a pipeline meant to be advanced stage-by-stage through bootstrap itself, but the actual mechanism for advancing anything past vision is not in bootstrap at all - it's the separate intent assess / workflow start|advance / design import / planning show|handoff command families, which have no automatic linkage back to the bootstrap manifest (see the bootstrap-approve-verb issue). We had to infer the entire bootstrap defines what artifacts exist; intent/workflow/design/planning are how you produce and advance them; gates are a manually-maintained checklist over the result model purely from reading dist/cli.js source, since no doc walks through this relationship end-to-end. A new user following only the public docs would reasonably expect bootstrap itself to have subcommands for architecture/design/data/security (mirroring its vision-stage subcommands: vision-amend, vision-check, vision-approve) and would be confused to find it doesn't. Fix: a short How the bootstrap pipeline works end-to-end doc section explaining (1) bootstrap tracks artifact status only, (2) intent assess/workflow/design/planning are the actual production mechanisms for each artifact, (3) gates require manual approval today (or automatic approval once bootstrap approve lands) tying the two together.

issues.name: clarify-use-command-project-lifecycle-mutation-gate
issues.description: autoforge use <alias> <command> rewrites args to --project <path> <command> and dispatches against that project directory (src/cli entrypoint, main()). projectMutationBlocked() (src/workspace/lifecycle.ts) blocks any command not in readOnlyCommands (help, version, doctor, projects, assets, agents, bootstrap, twin, evidence) unless the target project's metadata.lifecycle === active. For a project registered via bootstrap attach/projects register without lifecycle ever having been explicitly set, metadata.lifecycle is undefined - not active - so it silently falls into the blocked branch, and every mutating command (add, decide, context, check, intent assess --persist, workflow start/advance, etc.) returns a bare Project lifecycle is undefined; mutating command "<cmd>" is blocked with exit code 4 and zero indication that autoforge projects update <path> --lifecycle active is the fix. We hit this immediately when trying to use autoforge use to file issues against the autoforge project itself - it had been registered but never had lifecycle set. This is a reasonable safety default but is currently undiscoverable: nothing in bootstrap attach, projects register, or projects show's output mentions that a freshly-registered project defaults to a locked, read-only-mutation state, or names the exact --lifecycle active fix. Fix: (1) have bootstrap attach / projects register set lifecycle: active by default rather than leaving it undefined, since an explicit opt-in gate that's silently on by default provides no real safety benefit; or if the undefined-as-blocked default is intentional, (2) print the exact fix command in the blocked-command error message instead of just the current lifecycle value.

issues.name: implement-documentation-gate
issues.description: Add decision-kind tagging, a done-time documentation gate for issues/tasks, and autoforge changelog compile, per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-documentation-gate-design.md.

issues.name: implement-v0-22-learning-evidence-engine
issues.description: Add hypothesis, experiment, and evidence domains, close the loop via decide --evidence, and expose all three through the digital twin, per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-v0-22-learning-evidence-design.md.

issues.name: surface-evidence-in-why-search
issues.description: The v0.22 Learning & Evidence Engine design spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-v0-22-learning-evidence-design.md, section 2) specifies that autoforge why's formatDecisionMatches() should include an 'Evidence: <id>, <id>' line when a matched decision has evidence records pointing at it via resultingDecision -- surfacing the concrete evidence that prompted a decision, not just its own reasoning text. This was never implemented: no task in the v0.22 implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-22-v0-22-learning-evidence.md) covers src/decisions/search.ts, confirmed by the final whole-branch review as a design-to-plan scope gap, not an implementation defect. The underlying data is correctly recorded (Evidence.resultingDecision is correctly stamped by decide --evidence, verified end-to-end in the self-hosted exercise), but is not yet readable through the primary human/agent-facing query command. Fix: load evidence records in runWhyCommand, group by resultingDecision, and append an Evidence: line to each matched decision block in formatDecisionMatches() when applicable. This closes the read half of the loop -- v0.22 currently delivers loop INTEGRITY (data is correctly linked) but not yet loop VISIBILITY (the data isn't surfaced through autoforge why).

issues.name: global-install-primary-onboarding-path
issues.description: README, CONTRIBUTING, and QUICKSTART taught npm install --save-dev + npx as the primary install path, contradicting the already-current onboarding docs which assume a globally installed CLI. QUICKSTART.md also described an entirely different, older AutoForge product (autopilot/recipes/training-loop commands that don't exist).

issues.name: onboarding-prompts-default-to-init-not-attach
issues.description: The canonical onboarding prompt (README, agent setup guide) told agents to initialize or attach a project only when needed, phrased as an either/or. Agents reasonably ran autoforge init alone, which only creates local .autoforge/ state -- it never calls registerProject, so the project never appears in autoforge projects list. Reported by the user after observing this exact failure mode.

issues.name: Gate check omits active work id from evidence
issues.description: autoforge gate check never attached the active work item's id to recorded validation evidence, so the v0.24 why-integration (Task 6) could never surface a Validation line in practice; the twin's trace-link node type was also undocumented as edge-only, misleading the CLI reference.

issues.name: Add full capability map to agentic AI guide
issues.description: AUTOFORGE_AGENTIC_AI_GUIDE.md covered workflow etiquette only, predating v0.23/v0.24, with no map of the full domain surface (strategy, learning, governance, twin, orchestration, traceability). Added a Full Capability Map section explaining when to reach for each domain.

issues.name: Audit v0.25 Protocol and Core release candidate
issues.description: Read-only release audit of Protocol and Core manifests, public exports, schemas, dependency boundaries, tests, root publication wiring, and release documentation before committing or publishing v0.25.

issues.name: Repair v0.25 release automation for pnpm and dependency order
issues.description: Release Verification still runs npm ci with no package-lock, and CI's isolated root tarball install resolves unpublished Protocol/Core/SDK dependencies from npm. Convert release automation to pnpm, verify every public package artifact, and enforce the documented Protocol -> Core -> SDK -> Core CLI publication order.

issues.name: Introduce Changesets and complete v0.25 release metadata
issues.description: The accepted package policy and publication gate require Changesets, package-level release notes, changelogs, and compatibility ranges, but the repository has no .changeset configuration or release entries. Add the independent-version release workflow before publication approval.

issues.name: Enforce repository-relative scope in agent handoffs
issues.description: agentHandoffSchema rejects unsafe changedFiles but currently accepts absolute and parent-traversing scope include/exclude patterns. Reuse a canonical repository-relative scope schema and add focused rejection tests so canonical tracked handoffs cannot grant scope outside the repository.

issues.name: Reconcile Core CLI workspace ownership before v0.25 release
issues.description: The accepted architecture requires a private repository root and a publishable apps/core-cli package owning @cojacklabs/autoforge, but the root remains the public package and apps/core-cli has no manifest. Complete the relocation or explicitly amend the accepted policy and release readiness claims before tagging.

issues.name: Final v0.25 release candidate audit and deep validation
issues.description: Perform a read-only, release-blocking audit of the accumulated v0.25 worktree: repository hygiene, public API and package boundaries, security and credentials, compatibility, CI and release workflows, package artifacts, Changesets metadata, documentation consistency, and complete validation. Record every blocker before any commit, tag, GitHub release, npm publication, or deployment.

issues.name: Fix Windows AutoForge Agent launcher execution
issues.description: Release blocker: the public Core launcher resolves autoforge-agent.cmd on Windows but passes it directly to child_process.spawn with shell disabled. Node documents that .cmd files require cmd.exe or an equivalent shell, so bare Agent launch and the credentials proxy cannot work on Windows. Add real Windows process coverage while preserving argument safety, signals, exit codes, and recursion prevention.

issues.name: Harden experimental Agent path containment and entrypoint portability
issues.description: Release blocker for the Agent: LocalAgentWorkspace allows writes through a symlinked directory outside the project, and the import.meta.url entrypoint check silently skips main when the installed path contains spaces. Enforce real filesystem containment without TOCTOU/symlink escape, use a robust executable-entry check or bin shim, add regression tests, and reconcile npm installation documentation with the package's private release state.

issues.name: Eliminate generated-output race from CI boundary validation
issues.description: Release blocker: Turborepo boundaries scans ignored dist output after builds; the current CI schedules build and boundaries together, making the result order-dependent. Ensure authoritative source-only boundary validation and order CI so generated artifacts or restored caches cannot create false failures.

issues.name: Repair AutoForge project quality gate execution and file selection
issues.description: Release blocker: autoforge gate check cannot execute the configured bare tsc command from a normal environment, and an active all-scope issue selects no files so file containment, secret scanning, and structured syntax are skipped. Use package-manager-resolved commands and define reliable changed/scope file selection with regression coverage.

issues.name: Prepare reviewable v0.25 release checkpoint and remote verification
issues.description: After release blockers are fixed, split the accumulated worktree into bounded commits while excluding claude_resume.md and local .autoforge/learning/strategy.json, verify exact Changesets baseline/release-set metadata, push for Node 22 GitHub CI, re-run release verification, record explicit approval, and publish Protocol then Core then SDK then Core CLI. Do not tag or publish before every gate passes.

issues.name: Define and enforce an Agent code-commenting standard
issues.description: Post-v0.25 governance enhancement: require AutoForge-guided agents to leave durable, high-value code commentary where intent is not evident from implementation. Document and enforce comments for public API contracts, architectural boundaries, security and compatibility constraints, non-obvious algorithms, invariants, and intentionally unusual tradeoffs. Explicitly prohibit noisy comments that restate syntax, stale narrative comments, raw prompt transcripts, and unactionable TODOs. Prefer explain-why comments, typed APIs, tests, and decision links; require TODO/FIXME comments to reference an AutoForge work item when practical. Integrate the standard into generated agent context/contracts and review gates, with objective checks limited to enforceable surfaces such as exported API documentation rather than arbitrary comment-density quotas. Plan this after the v0.25 release checkpoint so it does not expand the current release candidate.

issues.name: Define optional Intent Compiler and portable design orchestration
issues.description: Backburner platform architecture: define provider-neutral contracts and boundaries for lightweight-model prompt compilation, clarification, task and memory proposals, explainable prioritization inputs, evidence-backed research assistance, and portable design contracts consumed through Figma, TypeUI, Stitch, and future adapters. Core must remain deterministic and own schemas, validation, governance, state, evidence, and approval; Agent or Service owns model routing and provider calls. This is not a v0.25 requirement, committed version, or fixed sequence. The preserved concept is docs/planning/0.25/FUTURE_INTELLIGENCE_AND_DESIGN_ORCHESTRATION.md.

issues.name: Enforce Agent generated-content safety before writes and streaming
issues.description: Add code-level validation and sanitization for model-generated file content and streamed output before the experimental Agent writes to disk or stdout. Reject secrets, raw transcripts, and machine-specific absolute paths; ensure failed validation cannot leave partial edits; and cover the policy with focused tests before Agent or Providers publication.

issues.name: Make release readiness use superseding gate evidence
issues.description: Preserve historical validation evidence while evaluating readiness from the latest applicable required result for each gate and work context, so corrected reruns can supersede earlier failures without deleting audit history.

issues.name: Document the post-v0.25 north-star roadmap
issues.description: Preserve the proposed v0.26 trust-and-portability charter, candidate later milestone sequence, architectural invariants, exit gates, and immediate implementation order as the authoritative planning starting point for development beyond v0.25.

issues.name: Adopt AutoForgeAI orchestration ideas into the north-star roadmap
issues.description: Document the independently reimplemented mission-control, role-specialized agent, atomic work claiming, dependency-aware parallelism, human-input, scheduling, live-progress, browser and terminal review, and recovery concepts observed in AutoForgeAI/autoforge; map each capability to AutoForge architectural owners and candidate milestones while prohibiting AGPL source copying and provider lock-in.

issues.name: Define and benchmark the hybrid SQLite storage boundary
issues.description: Design and benchmark a file-canonical, database-accelerated storage architecture: tracked Markdown and JSON remain authoritative project truth; optional SQLite stores must be rebuildable indexes or local operational Agent state with schema migrations, source fingerprints, deletion recovery, transactions, WAL where justified, retention policy, and SDK-only access. Do not add SQLite until measurable concurrency, query, scale, or latency evidence justifies it.

issues.name: Reconcile v0.26 priority and document the ultimate AutoForge AI north-star
issues.description: Make superseding validation evidence the explicit first v0.26 implementation priority, preserve commenting governance, Agent safety, hybrid storage, and intent/design work in ordered sequence, and create one authoritative ultimate north-star vision spanning provider-neutral project intelligence, first-party Agent, general-purpose personal and organizational AI, channels, connectors, memory, orchestration, storage, Service, Web, safety, and candidate delivery horizons.

issues.name: Make project status respect active strategy priority
issues.description: Reconcile project-status next-work recommendations with AutoForge strategy by ranking ready and planned tasks/issues by active now, next, later, backlog assessments before stable work-state order. Preserve deterministic fallback for unassessed and legacy projects, add focused status tests, and ensure the documented v0.26 evidence-first priority appears in the bare status command.
